subject: Improbable beta (b) coefficient after a 2pl model

messages.author: ea21f7bb0093ce5e
messages.subject: Improbable beta (b) coefficient after a 2pl model
parts:
I'm working with 5 variables related to "child and family health". My model is composed of items such as "Do you have a child with a learning or behavior problem?" and "Do you and your family members have health insurance or access to regular medical and dental care?" 
My well fitted into a 2PL model: TLI 0.92
However, the coefficients that I've obtained showed that one item (cf2) has the difficulty at 31.375. I'm not sure if something is going under my radar and I'm wondering if someone could explain me these results.

Results are:

$items a b g u cf1 1.778 1.885 0 1 cf2 0.096 31.375 0 1 cf3 1.434 3.113 0 1 cf4 1.830 0.328 0 1 cf5 1.206 1.876 0 1

The data is attached

The code I'm using is:

mod_2pl_cf <- mirt(data = dataset_esq%>% select(cf1:cf5),
                model = 1,  
                itemtype = "2PL"
                )

M2(mod_2pl_cf)

 coef(mod_2pl_cf, simplify=T,
     IRTpars= TRUE)

Thanks

messages.author: b330c2028fed415b
messages.subject: Re: Improbable beta (b) coefficient after a 2pl model
parts:
Your item looks rather difficult and has very low discrimination, so this makes sense to me. The inflection point doesn't happen until a very extreme latent trait level. Your third item is also difficult, but because the discrimination is much further from 0 you don't see this difficulty effect.


Phil
